automation_levers: 835 ERA RARC/CARC underpayment & ERISA plan classifier
FAIR Health / clinical-acuity baseball-arbitration brief builder
key_risks: Forfeited certified-IDR-entity fees on ineligible/state-regulated claims
Delayed payer remittance after prevailing IDR awards
regulatory_notes: Execute HIPAA Business Associate Agreements, screen federal ERISA vs state surprise-billing jurisdiction pre-filing, and comply with 42 U.S.C. § 300gg-111 / 45 CFR § 149.510 batching and cooling-off rules.
Calculate contingency fees strictly on incremental cash collected above the payer initial QPA payment net of unrecovered IDR fees.

inputs: Provider-authorized 835 ERA and 837 claim data, initial-payment or denial receipt dates, payer explanations, QPA disclosures, service codes, facility status, network status, and patient cost-sharing allocations under appropriate privacy and security agreements.

Plan funding and ERISA information, applicable state payment-dispute rules, emergency or nonemergency NSA eligibility facts, notice-and-consent records where relevant, and existing negotiation, IDR, or settlement histories.

Authorized-representative and counsel arrangements, current CMS procedures and certified-entity fee schedules, permissible batching criteria, negotiation/filing calendar, and a collection-based contingency agreement defining QPA and initial-payment treatment.
plays.mechanism: Ingest commercial out-of-network 835 ERA remittances for emergency, anesthesia, radiology, and eligible specialty surgical services, then screen federal No Surprises Act eligibility under 42 U.S.C. § 300gg-111 and related provider provisions against specified state-law or All-Payer Model rules; ERISA status is relevant but does not alone resolve jurisdiction. An authorized representative, with counsel where legal representation requires it, starts open negotiation within the applicable 30-business-day initiation window, completes the 30-business-day negotiation period, and initiates federal IDR within four business days afterward, batching only disputes that satisfy then-current federal criteria through a certified IDR entity. Charge 20%–30% only on incremental payer cash collected above the contractual QPA floor after nonreimbursed federal administrative and certified-entity fees, also excluding the initial payer payment from new recovery because QPA is a statutory benchmark rather than necessarily the initial payment; track evidence preparation and professional costs separately from submitted offers and awards.
metrics: Collectible dispute base: federally eligible disputed dollars with timely negotiation and IDR rights, separated from billed charges, requested offers, and unpaid awards.

Realized economics: incremental cash above both the initial-payment baseline and contractual QPA floor, net unreimbursed process fees, 20%–30% contingency receipts, and contribution after evidence and representative costs.
Process performance: timely initiation rate, eligible-batch acceptance rate, cost per resolved claim, days from determination to payment, and unpaid-award aging.
plays.name: Federal No Surprises Act Open-Negotiation and Certified-IDR Recovery Desk

platform_risks.detection_metric: Eligibility rejection rate, batch-separation rate, missed-deadline count, and nonreimbursed process cost as a percentage of incremental collections.
platform_risks.failure_mode: Jurisdiction, batching, or timing defects make an apparently profitable federal IDR submission ineligible.
platform_risks.fallback: Separate disputes only where still timely and permitted, use the applicable state process when available, continue permissible payer negotiation, and cease fee-generating submissions with negative expected net recovery.
platform_risks.impact: Disputes are dismissed or delayed, administrative and preparation expenses are stranded, and an award forecast never becomes incremental provider cash.
platform_risks.trigger: State-law review displaces federal IDR, services fail NSA eligibility, a batch violates current criteria, or negotiation and initiation timestamps miss applicable business-day deadlines.

workflow: 1. Reconcile each ERA to its underlying claim and initial-payment or denial receipt date; exclude ineligible services, route disputes governed by applicable state processes appropriately, and verify federal jurisdiction without assuming every ERISA or specialty-surgery claim qualifies.

2. Send the required open-negotiation notice within 30 business days after receipt of initial payment or denial, run the 30-business-day negotiation period, and assemble permissible evidence without using billed charges or prohibited public-payer comparisons.

3. Initiate federal IDR within four business days after negotiation ends, subject to applicable exceptions or extensions; form only currently permissible batches, select a certified entity, and meet offer, fee, and evidence deadlines rather than treating the initiation window as blanket batching authority.

4. Track settlements, determinations, payer payment deadlines, and actual deposits; calculate the fee base as max(0, cumulative comparable payer cash minus max(initial payer payment, contract-defined comparable QPA floor) minus nonreimbursed administrative and certified-entity fees), excluding patient collections and invoicing only after cash arrives.

plays.name: Out-of-Network Medical Claim & ERISA Appeal Contingency Recovery
plays.mechanism: Partner with surgical centers, air/ground ambulance operators, and specialty clinics to ingest underpaid or denied commercial insurance claims, automating federal No Surprises Act IDR (Independent Dispute Resolution) and ERISA administrative appeals on a 20–35% contingency fee.
inputs: Provider 835/837 EDI remittance & denial feeds (CO-45, CO-50, PR-96 codes)
Qualified Payment Amount (QPA) & regional FAIR Health benchmark database
Automated ERISA plan-document demand & Federal IDR portal filing workflow
workflow: Ingest denied and severely underpaid out-of-network commercial claims from specialty medical practices
Cross-reference payer remittances against statutory Open Negotiation windows (30 business days) under the No Surprises Act and ERISA SPD timelines
Generate evidence-backed arbitration briefs and ERISA appeals, collecting 20–35% of the incremental insurer payout above the initial remittance
metrics: Average incremental recovery per arbitrated claim ($1,500–$25,000+)
IDR / ERISA appeal win rate vs. initial payer offer (%)
Contingency revenue per practice partner per month

platform_risks.failure_mode: Missed 30-day Open Negotiation / 4-day IDR initiation statutory deadlines or HIPAA breach
platform_risks.trigger: Failing to file within strict federal No Surprises Act business-day windows or handling PHI without a signed Business Associate Agreement (BAA)
platform_risks.impact: Permanent forfeiture of IDR arbitration eligibility on expired claims or HIPAA compliance penalties
platform_risks.detection_metric: 100% BAA execution before EDI ingestion and automated T-minus-5-day statutory deadline alerts
platform_risks.fallback: Enforce HIPAA-compliant encrypted EDI pipelines with signed BAAs and fall back to longer-window ERISA administrative appeals when IDR windows have lapsed

plays.name: Out-of-Network DME, CGM & Diagnostic Reference Lab Billing Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Operating a healthcare Management Services Organization (MSO) and performance patient-acquisition engine that pairs targeted paid-social symptom funnels with independent telehealth physician groups and licensed Durable Medical Equipment (DME) / reference lab suppliers—acquiring insured patients at $85–$220 CAC for high-margin HCPCS/CPT codes (Continuous Glucose Monitors, pneumatic compression devices, home sleep testing, custom orthotics) that reimburse $900–$3,500+ against $70–$220 hardware COGS.
inputs: CMS DMEPOS Fee Schedule and commercial payer allowables matrix by HCPCS code and state MAC jurisdiction
Real-time insurance-eligibility and deductible verification API (Availity / Waystar / Stedi)
Compliant Management Services Organization (MSO) software + flat-fee marketing contracts with PECOS-enrolled DME suppliers and telehealth PCs
workflow: Run high-converting paid social and search funnels educating commercially insured and Medicare-eligible patients on covered at-home medical devices (CGMs, lymphedema pumps, sleep apnea monitors)
Perform instant real-time eligibility and remaining-deductible checks via EDI 270/271 before scheduling any clinical intake
Route qualified patients to an independent physician practice for a legitimate synchronous/asynchronous telehealth evaluation and medical-necessity chart documentation
Fulfill the prescribed hardware and recurring monthly supply refills through a licensed DME entity, collecting Recurring Rental / Resupply reimbursements every 30–90 days
metrics: Verified insurance-eligible patient CAC ($85–$220) vs. 12-month LTV including recurring resupply fills ($1,800–$4,500)
First-pass clean claim acceptance rate (%) and days sales outstanding (DSO)
Physician medical-necessity chart audit pass rate (100% LCD/NCD criteria match)

platform_risks.failure_mode: Payer post-payment audit recoupment or Anti-Kickback Statute (AKS) per-referral fee scrutiny
platform_risks.trigger: Paying per-lead commissions tied to federal healthcare volume or submitting claims without complete Local Coverage Determination (LCD) chart notes
platform_risks.impact: MAC prepayment review hold or clawback of reimbursed claims
platform_risks.detection_metric: 100% automated LCD clinical-criteria checklist validation before claim EDI 837P submission and strict flat-fee MSO billing
platform_risks.fallback: Structure all marketing and software agreements strictly under Safe-Harbor Personal Services / MSO flat fair-market-value retainers, prioritize commercial payers and recurring CGM resupply, and enforce third-party clinical chart review

plays.name: 340B Contract-Pharmacy & Covered-Entity Drug Price Spread Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Partnering with HRSA-qualified 340B Covered Entities (Federally Qualified Health Centers, Ryan White clinics, disproportionate-share rural hospitals) to provide turnkey Third-Party Administrator (TPA) split-billing software, specialty contract-pharmacy fulfillment, and tele-referral capture—buying outpatient specialty medications at 25–50%+ statutory 340B discounts while collecting 100% full commercial insurance reimbursement and splitting the multi-thousand-dollar per-script margin via compliant flat administrative/dispensing fees.
inputs: HRSA OPAIS (Office of Pharmacy Affairs Information System) database of Covered Entities and registered contract pharmacies
340B split-billing / virtual-inventory accumulator software tracking 11-digit NDCs, prescriber NPIs, and patient-eligibility encounters
Licensed specialty/mail-order contract pharmacy network and commercial payer PBMs
workflow: Identify under-monetized 340B Covered Entities (FQHCs, grantees, rural hospitals) with low specialty capture rates in the HRSA OPAIS registry
Deploy split-billing TPA software and mail-order specialty contract-pharmacy infrastructure that captures commercially insured prescriptions written or co-managed by clinic providers
Reimburse the pharmacy at full commercial payer rates ($3,000–$12,000/script) while replenishing drug inventory via the clinic's 340B wholesaler account at $800–$4,000/script
Charge fixed fair-market-value per-dispense administrative, software, and clinical-management fees that capture a major share of the net spread while funding the clinic's safety-net mission
metrics: Captured commercially insured 340B scripts per month per Covered Entity
Gross commercial-to-340B acquisition spread ($1,500–$6,000+) per specialty fill
HRSA audit pass rate (zero duplicate Medicaid discount or diversion findings)

platform_risks.failure_mode: Manufacturer contract-pharmacy restriction policies or HRSA 'patient definition' audit findings
platform_risks.trigger: Drug manufacturers restricting 340B replenishment to a single contract pharmacy unless claims data is submitted, or filling scripts for patients without a documented clinic encounter
platform_risks.impact: Loss of 340B ceiling price on specific NDCs or HRSA repayment liability
platform_risks.detection_metric: 100% EHR encounter-to-NPI match verification prior to 340B replenishment accumulation and automated ESP (340B ESP) data submission
platform_risks.fallback: Operate an in-house entity-owned specialty pharmacy location alongside contract pharmacies, automate 340B ESP claims-data uploads to unlock restricted NDCs, and enforce strict EHR encounter gates

inputs: Public Form 5500 filings and available Schedule A/C records, employer size and plan-year information, employer-confirmed renewal dates and appropriately obtained business contact details.

Employer authorization, incumbent fee disclosures, plan documents, aggregate claims and pharmacy reports, stop-loss terms, underwriting requirements and privacy-controlled access to necessary participant information.

Licensed broker and specialist relationships, TPA and stop-loss proposals, captive participation terms, PBM rebate and spread definitions, NADAC availability and fallback pricing rules, and a $40–$65 PEPM service proposal.
plays.mechanism: Use public Form 5500 Schedule A/C information, where filed and informative, to identify mid-market renewal and compensation-review opportunities, then offer an employer-authorized CAA 2021 service-provider fee-disclosure review. A properly licensed advisory team can seek broker-of-record appointments and compare bundled coverage with separately contracted TPA, stop-loss or suitable captive arrangements and a transparent pass-through PBM using an explicitly defined NADAC-based pricing methodology. Negotiate recurring $40–$65 PEPM advisory fees where supported by scope and client agreement, with all commissions and indirect compensation disclosed and no assumption that unbundling guarantees savings.
metrics: Recurring advisory revenue: enrolled employees multiplied by the contracted $40–$65 PEPM fee, less servicing costs and disclosed fee offsets.
Risk-adjusted employer cost: claims, administration, stop-loss premiums, pharmacy costs, collateral and runout obligations minus realized rebates and recoveries.
Service and retention quality: renewal retention, disclosure completeness, pharmacy guarantee reconciliation variance and unresolved participant access issues.
plays.name: Mid-Market Level-Funded Benefits and Transparent PBM Advisory Operator

platform_risks.detection_metric: Adverse-scenario funding gap, claims-to-budget variance, unrecovered stop-loss balances and unexplained differences between disclosed and received compensation.
platform_risks.failure_mode: The proposed unbundled plan produces adverse claims exposure or undisclosed compensation despite appearing cheaper on headline premiums.
platform_risks.fallback: Retain or competitively rebid the existing structure when risk-adjusted economics are unfavorable, obtain explicit pricing fallbacks and narrow the engagement to disclosed advisory work until implementation conditions are satisfied.
platform_risks.impact: Employer costs exceed projections, coverage continuity deteriorates and advisory fees or the BOR relationship become disputed.
platform_risks.trigger: Incomplete claims data, stop-loss lasers or exclusions, nonrefundable captive collateral, ambiguous PBM rebate definitions or unsupported NADAC pricing for uncovered products.

workflow: 1. Analyze publicly available filings through permitted access methods, identify likely renewal opportunities and confirm current plan arrangements directly because filings are historical and may omit relevant compensation details.
2. Obtain employer authorization, review applicable CAA 2021 disclosures and existing termination terms, and define advisory deliverables and compensation before requesting any BOR appointment.

3. Compare fully insured and level-funded options using expected and adverse claims scenarios, stop-loss exclusions and lasers, captive collateral, TPA fees, pharmacy guarantees and rebates actually retained by the employer.

4. Implement the employer-selected structure with licensed parties, privacy safeguards and continuity planning; collect agreed PEPM fees and review total costs, disclosures and service performance at each renewal.

plays.name: Automated Form 8850 WOTC (Work Opportunity Tax Credit) & Section 41 R&D Contingency Engine
plays.mechanism: Automate employer-authorized WOTC screening and separately substantiate Section 41 research credits, earning outcome-linked service fees only where permitted; program authorization, qualifying activities, wage coordination, and professional fee restrictions govern each claim.

Substantiated credits realized by the employer
Net permitted service fees after review and filing costs

plays.mechanism: Crawl target commercial domains and DNS TXT/CNAME records weekly to detect the exact day a company installs or removes high-ticket enterprise software tags (Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, Segment, NetSuite), predicting annual renewal windows (Month 10–11) and active vendor migrations.

B2B executive contact graph & migration-agency/SaaS partner routing

Route renewal-window and active-churn signals to competing SaaS sales teams, software resellers, and implementation agencies

Outbound reply-to-demo conversion rate on Month-10 renewal targets
Per-opportunity bounty or retainer revenue per agency/SaaS partner

plays.name: Subsidized / Developer-Tenant Multi-Inbox Cold Outbound Infrastructure
plays.mechanism: Provisioning hundreds of isolated secondary domains across subsidized Microsoft 365 developer/partner tenants, Cloudflare Email Routing, and low-cost SMTP relays—sending strictly 15–25 plain-text emails per inbox per day across 300+ free/subsidized mailboxes to deliver 150,000+ monthly B2B cold emails into primary inboxes without paying $6–$12/seat retail Google Workspace pricing.
inputs: Lookalike secondary domain portfolio with automated SPF, DKIM (2048-bit), DMARC (`p=quarantine`/`reject`), and custom tracking-free MX records
Subsidized M365 partner/developer tenants, Cloudflare Email Routing catch-alls, and distributed SMTP sending nodes
Automated peer-to-peer warmup network and master unibox reply-routing webhook
workflow: Provision 100–300 secondary sending domains and bind 2–3 mailboxes per domain via automated DNS and tenant scripts
Warm every mailbox for 14–21 days with realistic thread-depth conversations before introducing live outbound prospects
Cap daily outbound volume at <=20 zero-link, zero-tracking-pixel plain-text messages per mailbox per day to stay completely beneath ESP volume heuristics
Aggregate all prospect replies into a single unified AI-triaged inbox that books qualified B2B sales calls on pay-per-show or retainer terms
metrics: Primary-inbox placement rate (%) across Gmail and Microsoft 365 seed tests
All-in monthly infrastructure cost per 10,000 delivered plain-text emails ($)
Positive reply rate (%) and booked meetings per 1,000 prospects contacted

platform_risks.failure_mode: Tenant-wide outbound throttling or domain-footprint blacklisting (Spamhaus DBL)

platform_risks.impact: Tenant suspension or domain-level spam-folder routing
platform_risks.detection_metric: Daily seed-list inbox placement (%) and bounce rate (<1.5% hard threshold)
platform_risks.fallback: Enforce max 2–3 domains per tenant, strip all open/click tracking pixels, verify 100% of leads via SMTP catch-all checks before sending, and keep hot-standby warmed domains ready for instant swap
